title: Voronoi-border (b)⇒(a): fixed segment may cross Z at a codim-≥2 face

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
In Theorem (Voronoi-border characterization), direction (b)⇒(a), the proof fixes $x\notin Z$, $m=\nu_S(x)$ and walks along the FIXED straight segment $\sigma(t)=(1-t)x+t\,x_m$. At the first label-changing crossing it claims the segment passes through a shared $(m-1)$-facet, so the flanking cells $R_p,R_{p'}$ are Voronoi-adjacent and $p\in\partial T\subseteq I_S$.

**Gap.** Only generically true. A straight segment can pass exactly through a Voronoi vertex/edge (codim $\ge2$ face), where the two flanking cells meet ONLY at that face and are NOT Voronoi-adjacent (no shared facet); then $p\in\partial T$ does not follow. General position makes vertices simple but does not stop the GIVEN segment (with $x$ fixed off $Z$, $x_m$ a fixed prototype) from hitting one.

**Fix.** Restrict to the full-measure set of base points $x$ whose segment to $x_m$ meets only facets transversally (complement is null; $h_S=h_T$ a.e. suffices), or use a generic descent path that crosses only facets, or a path-free argument.
